title: KaliBench: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Cybersecurity Tool Use on Kali Linux with Runtime-Free Verifiable Rewards
why_read: A rigorous benchmark exposing how poorly current LLMs translate natural language into exact, correct command-line security tool invocations.
analysis: KaliBench is a large benchmark of over 8,500 query-to-command pairs covering 1,642 real cybersecurity tools on Kali Linux, testing whether LLMs can generate exactly correct CLI commands rather than just reason abstractly about security concepts. The finding that no open-weight model exceeds 42% exact-command accuracy highlights a real and underappreciated gap between LLM 'knowledge' and precise executable output, which matters for anyone building security automation agents. It also shows that fine-tuning a small 8B model on this benchmark's verifiable rewards can match a much larger 685B model, which is a useful practical result for efficient model training. This is a solid, concrete contribution to both security tooling and LLM evaluation methodology.
